Saw-toothed grain beetle (Oryzaephilus surinamensis).

Description: a small, flattened beetle, roughly 2.5-3 mm long, brownish, with distinctive saw-tooth-like projections along the sides of the thorax (pronotum).

Damage: this species can squeeze through very small cracks or openings in packaging and sealed containers, attacking a wide range of stored products; it is considered a serious pest of stored grain and cereal products, and can also damage packaging materials by chewing through them.
